label: <DEL> step (sparse, strongest) + q as first token
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) The <DEL> step (t == L), about 50% of activation mass and all of the top activations (up to 0.27), but it fires on only about 5% of <DEL> steps. It is more likely for longer sequences (L >= 8) and when the first token, the one about to be output, is 2/i/k/h/o/m/u/w. I could not find a predicate that says which <DEL> steps fire. (2) Input q at t=0 always fires (precision 1.0 on dev) with a fixed, moderate value (about 0.046, 0.17 of max), about 23% of mass. Weaker leftovers: q at other positions (12% rate), y and a inputs, and the first copy step. It is mostly silent elsewhere in the original and copy phases. The disjunction has high mass recall but very low precision because most <DEL> steps do not fire.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=0 & in_tok=q (+8.52), t=1 & prev_tok=s (+6.17), t=1 & prev_tok=v (+5.12), t=1 & prev_tok=z (+4.94), in_tok=y (+4.08), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+3.41). Lower it: next_out=q (-4.38), next_out=y (-4.31), out_tok=q (-3.90), out_tok=y (-3.69).
